entities.name: Lorenzo Marcello
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lorenzo Marcello (1603–1656) was a Venetian patrician admiral whose career spanned Adriatic operations against the Papal fleet and the long Cretan War (1645–1669) against the Ottoman Empire. After service as provveditore and squadron commander, he succeeded to Captain General of the Sea in 1655, replacing Francesco Morosini at the head of Venice’s main armada.

In June 1656 he led a Venetian–Maltese fleet into the Dardanelles to intercept an Ottoman relief force bound for the siege of Candia. During the fighting on 26 June he was killed by cannon fire while pressing an attack; command passed to Barbaro Badoer, and the allies won a crushing victory—often ranked as Venice’s greatest naval success since Lepanto—destroying or capturing most of the Ottoman fleet and freeing thousands of Christian galley slaves.

Marcello’s death in victory made him a civic hero: his body was returned to Venice for state honours, while the temporary blockade of the Straits briefly starved Constantinople and stiffened Venetian resistance in Crete.
